submissions.title: Governor Abbott Directs Comprehensive Data Center Audit
submissions.excerpt: Any project that fails to comply with the requirements set forth by the PUC and ERCOT... must be denied connection to the Texas grid.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Gov. Abbott directed PUCT and ERCOT on Aug 3, 2026 to conduct a 'comprehensive verification and audit' of all data center projects in the ERCOT large-load interconnection queue (~474 GW of requests, ~90% attributed to data centers), pausing new interconnection approvals until developers disclose tax incentives, power/water use, and ownership. Statewide, not tied to one project, but directly relevant to numerous tracked UNDER_CONSTRUCTION/ANNOUNCED Texas projects (e.g. Cipher Black Pearl, Crusoe Goodnight, Fluidstack Abernathy, IREN Childress, IREN Sweetwater, Meta El Paso, Nscale Barstow, QTS-Lancium Hall County, Stargate Milam County, Stargate Shackelford County, Abilene Clean Campus). Corroborated by Texas Tribune, Utility Dive, E&E News, National Law Review. Reviewer should judge whether/how to attach to individual project timelines.

claims.methodology: Total ERCOT large-load interconnection queue cited in the Governor's letter; ~90% attributed to data centers per secondary coverage, not a single-project figure.

submissions.title: Louisville committee advances 6-month data center moratorium to Metro Council
submissions.excerpt: Planning and Zoning Committee voted 7-1 Tuesday to move the proposal forward to the full council for approval.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Louisville Metro Council's Planning & Zoning Committee voted 7-1 on Aug 4, 2026 to advance a 180-day moratorium on new hyperscale data centers (barring facilities over 500,000 sq ft, restricting others to industrial zoning), backed by Mayor Craig Greenberg. Full Metro Council vote scheduled for Aug 13, 2026 -- not yet enacted as of this submission. Not tied to a specific tracked project. Corroborated by LPM, Kentucky Lantern, LouisvilleKY.gov council statements.

submissions.title: Hyperscale data center, natural gas-fired project planned for Paducah's former nuclear plant
submissions.excerpt: Targeting more than 1.2 GW of compute capacity and dedicated on-site power generation built specifically for the project.
submissions.note: New project, not currently tracked: Brookfield and NextEra Energy announced (~Jul 29, 2026) a data center campus at DOE's former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant site, McCracken County, Kentucky -- Brookfield to develop/operate, NextEra to build dedicated on-site generation (reported up to 2 GW gas + 2.6 GW battery storage) supporting up to 1.8 GW of utility-delivered capacity by 2032; initial operations targeted 2028. Total investment reported at roughly $100B over time -- flagged LOW confidence as this is a multi-phase, multi-source estimate, not a single stated capex figure from a primary filing. Announcement is ~10 days old at time of this submission (outside the usual 24-72h window) but the project does not appear in the current 103-project tracked list, so flagging as a coverage gap.

claims.methodology: Initial targeted compute capacity as reported in company statements relayed by multiple trade/local outlets; primary company release not independently fetched this run.

Roughly $100B total investment 'over time' cited across secondary coverage; likely a multi-phase lifetime ambition figure rather than committed capex, analogous to other campuses in this tracker -- reviewer should treat as directional only.

submissions.title: Galaxy Expands Data Center Footprint with Acquisition of 500 Acre Campus in McGregor, Texas
submissions.excerpt: Expected to reach 74 MW in its first phase before expanding into a multi-hundred-megawatt campus.
submissions.note: New project, not currently tracked (distinct from the already-tracked 'Galaxy Helios' project). Galaxy Digital acquired 500 acres in McGregor, Texas (~90 miles north of Austin) for a second Texas AI/HPC campus, internally called 'Project Merlin' during city council review. First phase ~74 MW targeted to begin receiving power in 2028, privately funded substation, with potential expansion toward 500 MW as transmission is upgraded (initial phase kept under ERCOT's 75 MW large-load threshold). Directly relevant to the new Aug 3, 2026 statewide ERCOT interconnection audit/pause (see separate submission) since this is a new ERCOT-queue Texas project. No confirmed capex disclosed -- left blank per policy.

claims.methodology: Initial phase capacity as stated in Galaxy's own press release/local coverage of the McGregor site acquisition.

submissions.title: Democratic lawmakers propose three-year moratorium on new large data centers in Oregon
submissions.excerpt: Four ... lawmakers ... propose a three-year moratorium on new data centers in the state.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Four Oregon Democratic state legislators (Sens. Golden, Neron Misslin; Reps. Munoz, Chaichi) announced Aug 4, 2026 intent to introduce a bill for a three-year moratorium on new large data centers, to be filed in the 2027 legislative session (starts January). This is a proposal only -- not yet introduced as a bill or voted on. Related/earlier context: Oregon Legislature already passed a one-year pause on a data center tax incentive program (Mar 2026), and Hillsboro City Council passed a 120-day local moratorium. Not tied to a specific tracked project.
